1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable spacing around headings, labels, and body text.

2.why: No italics or all-caps appear in any instructions, and all text is broken into short one-to-two-sentence blocks.

3.why: The screenshots are all desktop-width; the single narrow card layout suggests it would reflow, but readability at a mobile screen size is not directly shown.

4.why: Most instructions are short and plain (e.g., 'Copy these codes now. Each code can be used once.'), though phrases like 'protected one-way verification values' and 'Provisioning value' are jargon.

5.why: The recovery code field shows an example placeholder 'ABCDE-23489', but the verification code and authenticator code fields show no example of the expected input.

6.why: No screen contains a long block of text; the longest instructions are two short sentences such as the 'Shown once' warning.

7.why: The manual setup secret, provisioning value, and recovery codes are rendered as selectable text (the secret in a filled input), so they can be copied, though no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative is shown; the banner explicitly instructs 'Add this value manually' and only the raw secret and otpauth URI text are offered.

9.why: The screenshots show standard input fields but give no evidence of autofill attributes or password-manager support, and the sign-in uses email and mobile number with no password field at all.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the step and a solid blue primary button, though the confirmed recovery-code screen displays two blue buttons at once, slightly diluting the primary action.

11.why: Most steps ask one action, but the recovery-code confirmation screen presents both 'Verify recovery code' and 'Generate replacement codes' buttons simultaneously, and MFA settings offers two actions side by side.

12.why: Actions produce plain feedback banners ('Authenticator created. Add this value manually.', 'Recovery code confirmed.', 'Authenticator MFA is active.'), with the next step generally surfaced as a new button, though 'what comes next' is sometimes only implicit.

13.why: Recovery codes can be re-requested via 'Regenerate recovery codes' and the error message invites retry, but codes are 'Shown once' with no reveal/hide option, regeneration consumes an existing code, and no resend option appears on the verification code screen.

14.why: The only observed error message is the generic 'Unable to complete this request. Please try again.', which does not state the problem, though it does suggest retrying and does not blame the user.

15.why: No countdowns or reading time limits appear on any screen, and the provisioning URI shows period=120, giving a generous 120-second window to enter authenticator codes.
